language_semantics_records.plain_language_meaning: An iterable is an object that can produce a sequence of values for for/of and spread-like consumers.
language_semantics_records.precise_behavior: An iterable has a Symbol.iterator method returning an iterator. An iterator has next() returning {value, done}. Built-in collections and strings are iterable; plain objects are not iterable by default.
language_semantics_records.syntax_or_api_shape: for (const x of iterable), [...iterable], obj[Symbol.iterator](), iterator.next()
language_semantics_records.why_it_matters: Iteration protocols connect arrays, maps, sets, strings, generators, async iteration, and custom data sources.
safe_refactor_notes: When materializing an iterable, consider one-shot/lazy behavior
Preserve iterator close behavior if implemented

language_semantics_records.plain_language_meaning: Generator functions make it easier to define iterators and lazy sequences.
language_semantics_records.precise_behavior: function* returns a generator object. yield produces a value and pauses execution. return, throw, and delegation with yield* affect control flow between consumer and generator.
language_semantics_records.syntax_or_api_shape: function* g(){ yield x; } const it = g(); it.next(); yield* other
language_semantics_records.why_it_matters: Generator control flow is bidirectional enough to surprise reviewers unfamiliar with pause/resume behavior.
common_misuse: Expecting function* body to run before next()
Using generator where a simple array is clearer
debugging_symptoms: Cleanup not run until iterator closed
safe_refactor_notes: Do not replace materialized arrays with generators without consumption tests
Document one-shot versus reusable iterable behavior

language_semantics_records.plain_language_meaning: A Promise represents a future fulfillment or rejection.
language_semantics_records.precise_behavior: A Promise settles once, either fulfilled with a value or rejected with a reason. then/catch/finally return promises and schedule handlers asynchronously according to the host event loop/microtask model.
language_semantics_records.why_it_matters: Promises structure async code but do not cancel work automatically or make ordering implicit.
safe_refactor_notes: Return promise chains from helper functions
Do not fire-and-forget without explicit reporting policy
language_semantics_records.runtime_or_environment: ECMAScript language core plus host async APIs

language_semantics_records.plain_language_meaning: async/await lets Promise-based code read like sequential code, while still returning promises.
language_semantics_records.precise_behavior: An async function always returns a Promise. await pauses the async function until the awaited value resolves or rejects. try/catch catches awaited rejections inside the async function, not unrelated async callbacks.
language_semantics_records.syntax_or_api_shape: async function f(){ const x = await p; return x; }
language_semantics_records.why_it_matters: async/await improves readability but does not remove rejection handling, cancellation, concurrency, or ordering design.
common_use: Bridge Promise APIs into clearer code
common_misuse: Forgetting that async function return value is a Promise
Awaiting operations sequentially that should run concurrently
Not awaiting a call whose rejection matters
debugging_symptoms: Caller receives Promise instead of value
safe_refactor_notes: Adding async to a function is API change unless callers already expect Promise
language_semantics_records.runtime_or_environment: ECMAScript language core plus host async APIs

language_semantics_records.plain_language_meaning: Async iteration consumes values that arrive over time.
language_semantics_records.precise_behavior: An async iterable has Symbol.asyncIterator and is consumed by for await...of. Each next step can await a Promise. It is useful for streams and paged/network-like sources.
language_semantics_records.syntax_or_api_shape: for await (const chunk of asyncIterable) { } async function* g(){ yield await x; }
language_semantics_records.why_it_matters: Async iteration combines iteration and async failure/lifecycle concerns.
common_use: Consume readable streams or paged async sources
common_misuse: Forgetting loop is async and needs await at caller
Buffering everything when streaming was intended
tests_or_checks: Test early break, error, and empty source
Check caller awaits enclosing async function
safe_refactor_notes: Do not convert async iterable to array unless bounded

async_records.runtime_or_environment: browser and Node host APIs plus ECMAScript functions
async_records.problem_addressed: Represent async completion or event notification without blocking.
async_records.behavior_explained: A callback is a function value passed to an API and invoked later by that API or host environment. The surrounding call usually returns before the callback executes.
async_records.safe_pattern: Name callback boundaries, keep callback small, and ensure the outer function does not claim to return callback-produced data synchronously.
async_records.dangerous_pattern: Returning a value from inside a callback and expecting the outer function to return it.
common_failure_modes: Outer function returns undefined or stale state
Exceptions occur outside expected synchronous control flow
Callback runs multiple times or never runs depending on API
diagnostic_questions: Which API invokes the callback and when?
Does the outer function return before the callback runs?
Can the callback run more than once?
tests_or_evidence_needed: Use a fake timer/event/source to prove ordering
Test zero, one, and multiple callback invocations

async_records.runtime_or_environment: primarily Node and callback-style host APIs
async_records.problem_addressed: Keep success and failure channels explicit for callback APIs.
async_records.behavior_explained: Many callback APIs report failure through an error argument or error event rather than throwing synchronously. Promise wrappers must translate that failure channel into rejection.
async_records.safe_pattern: Check the documented callback signature; handle error first where applicable; reject wrappers on error and resolve only on success.
async_records.dangerous_pattern: Ignoring the error parameter or throwing inside an asynchronous callback expecting an outer try/catch to catch it.
diagnostic_questions: What is the documented error path?
Is the error branch tested?
Does a wrapper settle exactly once?
tests_or_evidence_needed: Stub API to call callback with error
Test success and error cannot both settle

async_records.runtime_or_environment: ECMAScript language core plus host APIs
async_records.problem_addressed: Represent one eventual success or failure and compose async steps.
async_records.behavior_explained: A promise settles once. Handlers registered with then/catch/finally run asynchronously and return new promises. Returning a promise from a handler chains its settlement.
async_records.safe_pattern: Return promise chains from functions, attach catch at recovery/reporting boundaries, and use Promise.all/allSettled/race deliberately.
async_records.dangerous_pattern: Creating a promise chain but not returning it, or handling only fulfillment.
diagnostic_questions: Which promises are returned to the caller?
Where can each promise reject?
Which combinator matches desired failure semantics?

async_records.runtime_or_environment: ECMAScript language core plus host APIs
async_records.problem_addressed: Connect async transformations without nesting callback pyramids.
async_records.behavior_explained: then returns a new promise whose settlement depends on handler return/throw behavior. A thrown error rejects the next promise; a returned promise is assimilated.
async_records.safe_pattern: Keep chains linear; return nested promises; use catch near the boundary that can recover.
async_records.dangerous_pattern: Starting async work inside then without returning it, causing the chain to continue early.
diagnostic_questions: Does every then handler return the async work it starts?
Does catch cover the intended chain?
Are sync exceptions and rejected promises both handled?
tests_or_evidence_needed: Add a delayed promise in a handler
Assert final result waits for nested work
Test thrown error and rejected promise

async_records.runtime_or_environment: ECMAScript language core plus host APIs
async_records.problem_addressed: Prevent async failures from being lost or reported at the wrong boundary.
async_records.behavior_explained: A rejection propagates along a promise chain until an onRejected handler or catch handles it. async functions convert thrown errors into rejected returned promises.
async_records.safe_pattern: Handle rejection with await inside try/catch, returned catch chains, or top-level/reporting boundaries; rethrow when the caller must decide.
async_records.dangerous_pattern: catch that logs and continues with an invalid fallback, or missing catch for fire-and-forget work.
diagnostic_questions: Where is the rejection handled?
Can the handler recover or should it rethrow?
Is fire-and-forget explicitly reported?
tests_or_evidence_needed: Test rejection from every async dependency
Check logs/metrics path for intentional background tasks

async_records.runtime_or_environment: ECMAScript language core plus host APIs
async_records.problem_addressed: Make promise flows read sequentially without changing that the API is asynchronous.
async_records.behavior_explained: An async function returns a Promise immediately. Returning a value fulfills the promise; throwing rejects it; awaiting a promise pauses only the async function.
async_records.safe_pattern: Declare async only when callers can handle a Promise; document the Promise result; keep synchronous and asynchronous APIs distinct.
async_records.dangerous_pattern: Adding async to a formerly synchronous function without updating callers.
common_failure_modes: try/catch at caller fails unless await is used
diagnostic_questions: Who calls this function and do they await it?
Does adding async alter a public API?
Can the function still throw synchronously before returning?
tests_or_evidence_needed: Test caller without await fails in expected way

async_records.runtime_or_environment: ECMAScript language core plus host APIs
async_records.problem_addressed: Make dependencies explicit while preserving intended concurrency.
async_records.behavior_explained: await waits for one value before continuing. Multiple awaits in sequence serialize dependencies unless promises were started earlier. Promise.all starts/joins concurrent work but rejects on first rejection.
async_records.safe_pattern: Start independent work before awaiting; await dependent work in dependency order; use Promise.all or allSettled according to failure semantics.
async_records.dangerous_pattern: Sequential awaits for independent network/file operations, or missing await before returning data.
common_failure_modes: Race where result is used before ready
diagnostic_questions: Which operations truly depend on earlier results?
Which promises are started before await?
Should one failure stop all or report partial results?

async_records.runtime_or_environment: callbacks promises async await events streams
async_records.problem_addressed: Align error handling with the async abstraction in use.
async_records.behavior_explained: Synchronous try/catch catches thrown errors in the same call stack. Promise rejections are caught by await/catch. Event and stream errors often use event channels. Callback errors use callback conventions.
async_records.safe_pattern: Identify the abstraction first, then handle failure at its boundary and convert to the next abstraction deliberately.
async_records.dangerous_pattern: Putting one broad try/catch around code that starts callbacks/events/promises and assuming all later failures are caught.
diagnostic_questions: Is this failure thrown, rejected, emitted, messaged, or callback-reported?
Where is cleanup guaranteed?
Does conversion wrapper handle both success and failure exactly once?
tests_or_evidence_needed: Test sync throw, rejected promise, callback error, event error, and cleanup

async_records.runtime_or_environment: ECMAScript async iteration plus host async sources
async_records.problem_addressed: Process a sequence whose elements arrive asynchronously.
async_records.behavior_explained: for await...of awaits each next result from an async iterable. Errors during next or yielded promises reject/throw into the loop. Early exit may trigger iterator cleanup.
async_records.safe_pattern: Use for await for sequential chunk/page processing; wrap loop in try/catch/finally; avoid materializing unbounded streams.
async_records.dangerous_pattern: Using for...of on async iterable or collecting all chunks before processing unbounded input.
diagnostic_questions: Is the source async iterable or ordinary iterable?
Can the sequence be unbounded?
What happens on break or error?
tests_or_evidence_needed: Test empty, multiple chunks, delayed chunks, thrown error, and early break

async_records.problem_addressed: Schedule work after a delay or repeatedly.
async_records.behavior_explained: Timer APIs are host-provided. They schedule callbacks for later execution; delays are not precise guarantees of exact execution time, and ordering with other events/promises depends on host event loop behavior.
async_records.safe_pattern: Keep timer callbacks idempotent; clear timers when lifecycle ends; test with fake timers where appropriate.
async_records.dangerous_pattern: Using setTimeout as a synchronization guarantee for network/DOM/stream completion.
diagnostic_questions: What condition is the timer standing in for?
Who clears the timer?
Could callback run after state is invalid?

async_records.problem_addressed: Respond to user, document, network, and platform events.
async_records.behavior_explained: Event listeners run when the browser dispatches events. Propagation, default actions, listener options, and target/currentTarget shape matter.
async_records.safe_pattern: Attach listeners at clear lifecycle points; remove them if needed; inspect event target/currentTarget; prevent default only when appropriate.
async_records.dangerous_pattern: Assuming a handler runs immediately or only once, or assuming event.target is the element the listener was attached to.
common_failure_modes: Default action still happens or is wrongly prevented
diagnostic_questions: Where is listener attached and removed?
Does propagation matter?
Is target or currentTarget intended?

async_records.runtime_or_environment: browser host APIs and environments with compatible APIs only after verification
async_records.problem_addressed: Handle HTTP/network operations that return promises.
async_records.behavior_explained: Fetch-style APIs are asynchronous. A fulfilled promise may still represent an HTTP error status depending on the API; network failure, parsing failure, and application-level failure are separate.
async_records.safe_pattern: Await the response, check status/ok according to API docs, parse body once, and handle abort/timeout policy where supported and verified.
async_records.dangerous_pattern: Assuming any fulfilled networking promise means usable successful JSON data.
common_failure_modes: UI treats HTTP error page as success
diagnostic_questions: Which environment provides fetch?
Does this API reject on HTTP status or only network failure?
What prevents stale result use?
tests_or_evidence_needed: Mock HTTP 200, 400/500, malformed JSON, network failure, slow response, and aborted request

async_records.behavior_explained: Streams emit or consume chunks over time and have lifecycle, backpressure, error, and completion semantics.

async_records.runtime_or_environment: browser workers and Node worker threads after current verification
async_records.problem_addressed: Move work across threads/process-like boundaries using messages.
async_records.behavior_explained: Worker APIs communicate through message events or ports. Values crossing the boundary follow host cloning/transfer rules; code does not share ordinary object identity.
async_records.safe_pattern: Define message schemas, correlate requests/responses, handle error/exit/termination, and verify current worker API details.
async_records.dangerous_pattern: Mutating an object after sending it and expecting the worker/main side to see the mutation.
diagnostic_questions: What values cross the boundary?
How are errors and exits reported?
How are requests correlated?

async_integrity_policy.async_await_note: async/await improves readability for Promise flows but does not solve cancellation, ordering, unhandled rejections, callback errors, stream lifecycle, or worker message boundaries by itself.
